Satan (Doctrine)
SAY-tun
proper noun (demonology)
Hebrew satan (adversary, accuser); Greek satanas. The personal name and title of the chief of the fallen angels, the adversary of God and His people, also called the devil (diabolos, slanderer), the serpent, the dragon, the prince of this world, the god of this age, and the prince of the power of the air.

📖 Biblical Definition

Hebrew satan (adversary, accuser); the personal name and title of the chief of the fallen angels, the great adversary of God and His people. Scripture reveals Satan under many names and titles: the devil (Greek diabolos, slanderer, accuser; Matthew 4:1); that old serpent (Revelation 12:9, 20:2, recalling Genesis 3); the great dragon (Revelation 12:9); the prince of this world (John 12:31; 14:30; 16:11); the god of this world / age (2 Corinthians 4:4); the prince of the power of the air (Ephesians 2:2); Beelzebub, the prince of the devils (Matthew 12:24); the accuser of our brethren (Revelation 12:10); Apollyon / Abaddon (the destroyer, Revelation 9:11); the tempter (Matthew 4:3); the wicked one (Matthew 13:19, 38). The biblical doctrine of Satan: he is a real personal being, a fallen angel (the chief of the fallen angels); he fell from his original holy estate through pride and rebellion; he is the adversary who tempts (Genesis 3; Matthew 4; the temptation of Christ), accuses (Job 1-2; Zechariah 3:1; Revelation 12:10), deceives (Revelation 12:9, which deceiveth the whole world; 2 Corinthians 11:14, transforming himself into an angel of light), and seeks to devour (1 Peter 5:8, your adversary the devil, as a roaring lion, walketh about, seeking whom he may devour); he is a creature, not a rival deity (the dualistic error), under God's sovereign control (Job 1-2, Satan can act only within the bounds God permits); he was decisively defeated at the cross and resurrection (Hebrews 2:14; Colossians 2:15; 1 John 3:8); he is destined for final judgment in the lake of fire (Revelation 20:10). The patriarchal-Reformed reader holds the substantive biblical doctrine of Satan against both the rationalist denial (Satan as a mythological symbol of evil) and the dualistic exaltation (Satan as a near-equal rival to God). Satan is a real, personal, powerful, but created and defeated adversary, under the sovereign control of God and destined for certain judgment.

📜 Webster 1828 Definition

Hebrew adversary, accuser; the personal name and title of the chief of the fallen angels; the devil, the old serpent, the dragon, the prince of this world; a real personal being, fallen through pride, who tempts, accuses, and deceives; a creature under God's sovereign control, decisively defeated at the cross, destined for the lake of fire.

SATAN, proper n. (demonology; Hebrew satan, adversary, accuser; Greek satanas) The chief of the fallen angels, the great adversary of God and His people. Many names: the devil (slanderer); that old serpent and great dragon (Revelation 12:9); the prince of this world (John 12:31); the god of this age (2 Corinthians 4:4); the prince of the power of the air (Ephesians 2:2); the accuser of the brethren (Revelation 12:10); the tempter (Matthew 4:3). A real personal fallen angel; fell through pride and rebellion; tempts (Genesis 3; Matthew 4), accuses (Job 1-2; Revelation 12:10), deceives (2 Corinthians 11:14), seeks to devour (1 Peter 5:8). A creature under God's sovereign control (Job 1-2), not a rival deity; decisively defeated at the cross (Hebrews 2:14; Colossians 2:15); destined for the lake of fire (Revelation 20:10).

📖 Key Scripture

1 Peter 5:8 — "Be sober, be vigilant; because your adversary the devil, as a roaring lion, walketh about, seeking whom he may devour."

Revelation 12:9 — "And the great dragon was cast out, that old serpent, called the Devil, and Satan, which deceiveth the whole world."

Job 1:12 — "And the LORD said unto Satan, Behold, all that he hath is in thy power; only upon himself put not forth thine hand. So Satan went forth from the presence of the LORD."

Colossians 2:15 — "And having spoiled principalities and powers, he made a shew of them openly, triumphing over them in it."

⚠️ Modern Corruption

Satan is a real, personal, created, and defeated adversary under God's sovereign control; the corruptions are the rationalist denial (Satan as a symbol of evil) and the dualistic exaltation (Satan as a near-equal rival to God).

expand to see more

Satan as a doctrine is held against two opposing errors. The rationalist denial treats Satan as a mythological symbol of evil rather than a real personal being; this contradicts the substantive biblical witness (the Lord Jesus's personal confrontations with Satan in the temptation, Matthew 4; the consistent biblical presentation of Satan as a personal adversary who tempts, accuses, and deceives). The dualistic exaltation treats Satan as a near-equal rival to God, a co-eternal principle of evil locked in cosmic struggle with the principle of good (the Manichaean and Zoroastrian dualisms, and various popular semi-dualistic conceptions); this contradicts the biblical doctrine that Satan is a creature, a fallen angel, under God's sovereign control (Job 1-2, where Satan can act only within the bounds God permits), decisively defeated at the cross (Colossians 2:15), and destined for certain judgment (Revelation 20:10). The patriarchal-Reformed reader holds the substantive biblical doctrine: Satan is real, personal, powerful, and active — the believer must be sober and vigilant (1 Peter 5:8), resist him (James 4:7), and stand against his wiles (Ephesians 6:11) — but he is a creature, not a rival deity; under God's sovereign control; decisively defeated at the cross; and destined for the lake of fire. The believer's confidence is in the certain victory of Christ over Satan, not in fear of an exalted devil.
